reproduction_target: QTLIT, an R/Shiny web application that chains a fixed analysis pipeline: FASTQ quality check (ShortRead), reference-genome indexing and paired-end short-read alignment (gmapR GmapGenome / gsnap), variant calling and filtering (bcftools v1.13 mpileup/call/view), VCF plotting (vcfR), VCF filtering (rTASSEL), VCF-to-R/qtl cross-object conversion (incorporated custom script), segregation-distortion filtering, linkage-map construction (ASMap / MSTmap) and rendering (LinkageMapView), and QTL mapping (R/qtl scanone or CIM). The reproduction target is the tool's own pipeline as described in Materials and Methods; there is no case-study dataset or worked example whose results could be re-derived. No wet-lab work is reported.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation, read from 'Materials and methods > R packages / Workflow and methodology / Program overview' plus the Results walk-through of the two GUI tabs. Utility packages that only support other steps (rtracklayer for FASTA import/export, Rsamtools for BAM indexing, Biostrings, stringr, rvest, gridExtra, ggrepel, parallel, qtlhot phenotype input) are folded into the step they serve and are not separately verdicted. Phenotype summary statistics and plots are folded into C12 (QTL analysis) since the paper presents them as one 'Run Analysis' action. This is a tool paper: the pipeline is fixed in the app source, but no input dataset, worked example, or expected output is provided anywhere in the paper or the repository, so no step has a concrete re-runnable instance.

steps.label: Raw FASTQ quality check with ShortRead (Morgan et al. 2009); optional step before alignment, produces zipped QC folder (images, PDF, HTML report, base-call statistics)
Reference-genome auto-indexing with gmapR GmapGenome function, default settings base size 12 and k-mer size 15 (Wu et al. 2016)
Paired-end short-read alignment to the indexed reference with gmapR gsnap function, 'default options', producing BAM files
Variant calling with BCFtools mpileup and call (bcftools v1.13, Danecek et al. 2021) invoked via system command from R; mapping-quality and base-quality filter of 20
Variant filtering and per-sample merge: BCFtools view for PASSED-flagged biallelic SNPs at filtration quality > 30; individual variant files automatically merged for downstream analysis
VCF quality / depth-of-coverage plotting with vcfR (Knaus & Grunwald 2017): variant quality score counts and DP distribution

VCF filtration with rTASSEL (Monier et al. 2022): minimum site count, allele frequency default min 0.05 / max 1.0, heterozygosity default min none / max 0.1, optional removal of minor SNP states; all user-adjustable

VCF-to-R/qtl cross-object conversion via a custom R script stated to be incorporated into the Shiny app scripting, cited as https://github.com/RimGubaev/v_to_qtl/blob/master/vcf_to_qtl_converter.R; requires user-supplied parent A name for ABH allele coding
Segregation-distortion filtering of markers at p-value threshold 0.05 (user-definable), with plot generation

Linkage-map construction with ASMap (Taylor & Butler 2017) using the MSTmap clustering algorithm (Wu et al. 2008); user selects map function among Haldane, Kosambi, Carter-Falconer, Morgan; linkage-clustering p-value currently set to 1.0 and user-changeable; cross type user-set
Linkage-map rendering to downloadable PDF with LinkageMapView (Ouellette et al. 2018)

QTL mapping with R/qtl (Broman et al. 2003): user chooses single-locus scan (scanone) or composite interval mapping (cim) and the test-statistic method among EM, imputation, Haley-Knott or extended Haley-Knott regression; outputs phenotype summary statistics, distribution plots (histogram, boxplot, QQ, violin), genotype/marker plots and a LOD plot with significant markers labelled via ggplot2/ggrepel/gridExtra

headline.static_readiness: 0/12 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: All 12 computational steps floor at X on the Data axis, and this is the paper's defining gap rather than an artefact of strict reading: QTLIT is a tool paper that supplies no example dataset, no test FASTQ/VCF/phenotype files, no accession, and no worked case study whose output could be compared. The Data availability statement contains only the GitHub URL, and the repository holds ui.R / server.R / global.R / renv.lock / renv / www and a one-sentence README with no data directory. Under an inference-inclusive reading that granted a user-supplied input, the binding ceiling would move to Code and Version at 1 each - the source is public but the repository has 0 tags, 0 releases and 5 commits, so no exact revision corresponds to the manuscript, and renv.lock (R 4.5.0, Bioconductor 3.21, per-package versions) is only a Stage-1 claim - giving NI, not R-star. R-star for any step would additionally require a Stage-2 read of server.R/global.R against a real input.
headline.coverage: 12 computational steps assessed from Materials and methods prose plus the Results GUI walk-through; 0 wet-lab steps (W=0, no bench work reported). Code availability is implicit in the Data availability statement (the GitHub URL); there is no separate code-availability section and no data-availability content beyond that URL.

gaps.where: All 12 computational steps - inputs to the entire pipeline
gaps.missing: No dataset of any kind. The Data availability statement is the bare string 'https://github.com/TKM-Lab/QTLIT' (the code repository), and that repository contains no data directory, no example FASTQ/BAM/VCF, no phenotype CSV, no reference genome, and no expected output. No GEO/SRA/ENA/figshare/Zenodo accession appears anywhere in the paper. The manuscript reports no case study: Figures 3-5 show output plots but the underlying species, population and files are never identified.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a small worked example (subsampled FASTQ pair or a demo VCF plus phenotype CSV and a reference contig) in the repository or a Zenodo deposit, together with the expected output plots/tables, so the pipeline has at least one re-runnable instance.

gaps.missing: The repository is public and live (HTTP 200) and holds the full Shiny source, but it is not archived and not versioned: 0 tags, 0 releases, 5 commits, no Zenodo/Software Heritage DOI, no LICENSE file, and the manuscript cites only the bare repository URL with no commit hash or release. There is therefore no identifiable revision corresponding to the manuscript, and no licence granting reuse.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release matching the manuscript, archive it (Zenodo DOI or Software Heritage identifier), cite that identifier in the paper instead of the bare URL, and add a LICENSE file.

gaps.missing: renv.lock is present in the repository (R 4.5.0, Bioconductor 3.21, per-package versions such as ASMap 1.0-8), which is a genuine environment-lock CLAIM, but it is unvalidated at Stage 1 and it covers only the R layer. The non-R components of the pipeline are outside it: bcftools (pinned as v1.13 in prose but installed at system level), the GMAP/GSNAP binaries and index format behind gmapR, and the TASSEL Java runtime behind rTASSEL. No container image or digest, no conda/apt specification, and no OS specification beyond 'LINUX environment ... 128 GB RAM and 32 cores'.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a container with a recorded digest (or a conda/apt manifest) covering bcftools, GMAP/GSNAP and the Java runtime alongside renv.lock, and state the base OS; then validate that renv::restore() plus the container reproduces a run.

gaps.where: Version pins stated in prose (all steps)
gaps.missing: Prose pins are partial and indirect: bcftools v1.13 and RStudio v2023.12.1-402 are exact, but every R package (rtracklayer, ShortRead, gmapR, Rsamtools, vcfR, Biostrings, rTASSEL, ASMap, LinkageMapView, R/qtl, gridExtra, qtlhot, ggrepel, shiny) is named without a version in the text, deferred to 'a supplementary file' that is not resolvable from the JATS record. The prose also does not state the R version; only renv.lock does (4.5.0).
gaps.how_to_close: State the R version and the key package versions inline in Materials and methods, and cite renv.lock as the authoritative record rather than an unlinked supplementary file.

gaps.where: Step C8 - cited provenance of the VCF-to-R/qtl converter script
gaps.missing: The URL given in Materials and methods for the incorporated conversion script, https://github.com/RimGubaev/v_to_qtl/blob/master/vcf_to_qtl_converter.R, returns HTTP 404, and the owning repository github.com/RimGubaev/v_to_qtl itself returns HTTP 404. The provenance of a load-bearing format-conversion step is therefore unresolvable from the paper; whether the vendored copy inside server.R/global.R matches any published version cannot be checked at Stage 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Vendor the script into the repository with an explicit attribution header recording the original author, source commit and licence, and correct or drop the dead URL in the manuscript.

gaps.where: Steps C3, C10, C12 - parameters left to the interactive user
gaps.missing: Several determinative choices are described only as user-selectable with no value recorded for any concrete run: gsnap is run with unenumerated 'default options'; the linkage map function is chosen among Haldane, Kosambi, Carter-Falconer and Morgan with no stated default; the QTL model is chosen between scanone and cim and the test statistic among EM, imputation, Haley-Knott and extended Haley-Knott. Because the app writes no parameter manifest alongside its outputs (none is described), a completed run is not self-documenting.
gaps.how_to_close: Emit a machine-readable run manifest (all parameter values, package versions, input checksums) with every download bundle, and state the defaults explicitly in the manuscript.

gaps.missing: The README is a single sentence ('This is an R Shiny script for a ShinyApp QTLIT (http://http://14.139.229.202:8080/QTLIT). The UI can perform alignment, variant calling, linkage mapping and QTL analysis.') and contains a malformed doubled scheme in the URL. There are no installation instructions, no statement of required external binaries (bcftools, GMAP/GSNAP, Java), no renv::restore() guidance, and no usage example. The hosted instance is a bare IP endpoint (http://14.139.229.202:8080/QTLIT) with no institutional domain, no HTTPS and no stated availability guarantee, so the 'user interface version' offered in the Abstract is a fragile dependency.
gaps.how_to_close: Write an installation README covering system prerequisites and renv::restore(), fix the malformed URL, and host the instance behind a stable institutional DNS name with HTTPS, or provide a container that lets users run it locally.
